findings.message: Removing claim_project_id fixes the named orphan case by binding every stale claim to its key for good. That drops the variant the old code and the old test handled: a stale claim under which nothing was ever made can no longer move to another key. The claim is released only from promoteToDelivery's catch, and that release is best-effort (`.catch(logError)`). So a crash, timeout or failed release between claimPromotion and the create leaves the opportunity locked to that key, and the only way out is to create a project under it. Fix: when a stale claim's key differs, allow the takeover if `lookupKey(createKey(o.id, o.claim_key))` shows nothing was started or made under it. Do this inside the claim transaction, or have the idempotency record mark in-flight work, so the slow-create race does not come back.
findings.scenario: Promote PS-0150 with the mistyped key NWX. The process dies after claimPromotion commits and before withIdempotency runs. Two minutes later, promote PS-0150 with NWI → 'was being promoted as NWX; promote it with that key to finish'. The only way through is to create project NWX.

findings.message: The release decision is a check followed by a separate write. lookupKey reads in its own transaction, then releasePromotion runs, and nothing ties 'nothing was made' to the moment of release. If lookupKey reports a key, the claim is kept for good, even when the failure came after the create and will repeat on every replay. Examples: recordPromotion hits the opportunity_project unique index, or the client lookup fails. Every same-key retry replays the same project id and fails the same way, and every other key is refused, so the opportunity can never be promoted and nothing records it as stuck. Fix: if recordPromotion refuses a replayed project for a lasting reason, release the claim and flag the project, for example by voiding it through delivery's contract. Also make the release depend on the idempotency record inside the same transaction.
findings.scenario: Two won opportunities whose create returns the same project id, promoted one after the other. B's recordPromotion violates opportunity_project. lookupKey(B's key) is set, so the claim stays. A retry of B with the same key replays the same id and is refused again, and a retry with another key gets 'promote it with that key to finish'. B is stuck permanently.

findings.message: The previous finding asked for three variants of the shared-project race: sequential, concurrent, and through a resumed claim. Only the first two are here, so the resumed-claim row is missing. The test also checks only that one promotion wins. It never asserts what happens to the loser afterwards: whether its claim is released or the project flagged, and whether it can still be promoted. Add the resumed-claim row, and assert the loser's state after the race.
findings.scenario: Delete the resumed-claim handling of the unique index, or leave the loser's claim stuck. Both rows still pass, because they count only the 'ok' outcomes.

findings.message: The release path changed from 'no project object' to 'lookupKey finds nothing'. The only release test fails before the create is ever called: delivery already has CON, so the pre-check throws. No row covers a create that delivery itself refuses or that throws, which is the case where withIdempotency has run. So nothing shows the claim is given back there, or that a different key works afterwards. The old row 'a stale claim that made nothing gives way to another key' was deleted and not replaced. Add table rows where the create stub throws (validation, forbidden, thrown before commit), each followed by a promote with another key that must succeed.
findings.scenario: withIdempotency records a key for a failed create, or lookupKey returns non-null after a refused create. The claim is kept, and the next promote with another key is refused. No test fails.

findings.message: If lookupKey throws inside the catch block, its error replaces the original failure `e`. The caller then sees a database error instead of the real reason the promotion failed. Catch the lookup failure, log it as 'release not attempted (unknown)', and rethrow `e`.
findings.scenario: Delivery refuses the create, then lookupKey times out. The user sees the timeout instead of delivery's refusal.

findings.message: projectOf falls back to the requested key when delivery's result, or a replayed result, has no key. The link is then recorded under a key delivery never confirmed. Fail closed when the key is missing, as the code already does for the id.
findings.scenario: A replayed result with resourceId and no key links the project under input.key without checking it.

findings.message: The fix for the slow-create race now depends on withIdempotency handling two creates that run at the same time under the same createKey. No test exercises that case. The 'slow first attempt' test holds attempt A at the gate before create is ever called. So A's create only starts after B has already created and linked the project, and A just gets a sequential replay. The test would stay green if withIdempotency had no handling for a create already in flight: no reservation, no lock, no unique key. Fix: block the stub inside delivery's create (after the insert, before the commit), or hold a DB lock, so both creates are in flight together. Then assert that exactly one project exists and that both attempts end with the opportunity linked to it.
findings.scenario: A's create inserts project SLO and stalls before commit for more than 120 s. B resumes with SLO and calls create under the same key while A is still in flight. Whether B blocks, replays or makes a second project is untested. The current test passes either way.

findings.message: createKey identifies a promotion by opportunity and key only. A retry that resumes the claim with different inputs gets back the project from the first attempt, with that attempt's billing, name and client. The new input is silently ignored and the promotion reports success. Fix: either include a fingerprint of the create input in the idempotency record and refuse a replay whose input differs, or refuse a resume whose billing differs from what the claim recorded.
findings.scenario: The first attempt promotes PS-0140 as KEY with billing 'fixed', and the link fails. The user retries as KEY with billing 't&m'. The replay links the 'fixed' project and returns { projectKey: 'KEY' } with no error, so the opportunity is promoted with the wrong billing.

findings.message: A slow first attempt that has been overtaken gets 'is no longer claimed by this promotion; promote it again with SLO', even though the same-key retry already linked the opportunity to that same project. Following the advice then fails with 'already project SLO'. Fix: when the token doesn't match but the opportunity is already linked to input.projectId, return success, or say that it is done.
findings.scenario: From the slow-attempt test: `first` resolves to an error telling the user to promote again, but the opportunity is already promoted as SLO.
